title: Service Bus vs Event Grid vs Event Hubs
description: Pick the right Azure messaging service for commands, resource notifications, and telemetry streams.

data.text: A new order platform needs three things: (1) send a "reserve stock" command to the warehouse service, retrying until it succeeds; (2) react when a blob is uploaded or a resource is deleted; (3) ingest 50,000 IoT sensor readings per second into a stream processor. Which Azure services do you use?

Use **Azure Service Bus** for (1) — it delivers discrete *messages* (commands) with transactions, sessions, retries, and dead-lettering. Use **Event Grid** for (2) — it delivers lightweight *resource events* from Azure services and your own publishers with push delivery and filtering. Use **Event Hubs** for (3) — it is a partitioned *event stream* built for high throughput and replay, not per-message acknowledgement.

data.title: Service Bus — send a command
Event Grid — subscribe to blob events (Bicep)
Event Hubs — stream sensor readings

data.text: The three services have different delivery semantics. You cannot ask Event Grid to hold a command until a worker acknowledges it, and you cannot ask Service Bus to stream 50k events per second cheaply. Choosing on **delivery semantic** rather than on "which is newest" avoids painful rewrites later.
